def-ctrl1-linear-lqr-control-problem:
## Definition

Fix a finite horizon $T>0$, state and control dimensions $n,m\ge1$, and the real quotient space $L^2(0,T;\mathbb R^m)$ of measurable controls modulo equality almost everywhere ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]). Let $A\in L^\infty(0,T;\mathbb R^{n\times n})$ and $B\in L^\infty(0,T;\mathbb R^{n\times m})$ be equivalence classes, let $x_0,x_T\in\mathbb R^n$, and let $x_d\in L^2(0,T;\mathbb R^n)$. Let $U_c\subset\mathbb R^m$ be nonempty, compact and convex. The pointwise control set is
$$
\mathcal U_c:=\{u\in L^2(0,T;\mathbb R^m):u(t)\in U_c\text{ for almost every }t\}.
$$
Let $Q\in L^\infty(0,T;\mathbb R^{n\times n})$ and $R\in L^\infty(0,T;\mathbb R^{m\times m})$ be symmetric almost everywhere, with $Q(t)\succeq0$ and $rI\preceq R(t)\preceq MI$ almost everywhere for constants $0<r\le M<\infty$. Let $P\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric positive semidefinite. For each $u\in\mathcal U_c$, its state is the unique continuous solution of the Volterra equation
$$
x_u(t)=x_0+\int_0^t\big(A(s)x_u(s)+B(s)u(s)\big)\,ds.
$$
The same state equation is defined for every $u\in L^2(0,T;\mathbb R^m)$, and the running and terminal cost on that ambient space is
$$
J(u)=\frac12\int_0^T\!\left((x_u(t)-x_d(t))^TQ(t)(x_u(t)-x_d(t))+u(t)^TR(t)u(t)\right)dt+\frac12(x_u(T)-x_T)^TP(x_u(T)-x_T).
$$
The constrained problem minimizes this ambient functional over $\mathcal F$, where additional path or terminal constraints are represented by a nonempty convex weakly sequentially closed set $\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal U_c$; with no additional state constraints, $\mathcal F=\mathcal U_c$. “Weakly sequentially closed” means that every weakly convergent sequence in $\mathcal F$ has its weak limit in $\mathcal F$ ([[def-weak-convergence-of-nets-and-sequences]]). The definition asserts no optimizer or adjoint existence; the state-map well-definedness is supplied by [[lem-ctrl1-measurable-linear-ode-state-map]].
def-ctrl1-smooth-transcription-data:
## Definition

For pointwise numerical transcription on $[0,T]$, the data consist of an integer $n\ge1$, open sets $\Omega_x\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and $\Omega_u\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, a nonempty compact convex control set $U_c\subset\Omega_u$, an initial state $x_0\in\Omega_x$, a pointwise-defined vector field $f:[0,T]\times\Omega_x\times\Omega_u\to\mathbb R^n$, a pointwise-defined running cost $L:[0,T]\times\Omega_x\times\Omega_u\to\mathbb R$, and a terminal cost $\phi:\Omega_x\to\mathbb R$. The admissible state solves $\dot x(t)=f(t,x(t),u(t))$ almost everywhere and the continuous objective is $\int_0^T L(t,x(t),u(t))dt+\phi(x(T))$. Optional path and endpoint constraints are pointwise-defined functions evaluated at declared continuous times or transcription nodes. A **compact tube** is a compact subset of $[0,T]\times\Omega_x\times\Omega_u$ containing the state/control triples used by stages and trajectories. On such a tube, $f,L,\phi$ and any constraint functions used in a local NLP theorem are continuous and have continuous state/control derivatives through order three (the $C^3$ convention of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), with those derivatives bounded. An $L^\infty$ equivalence class alone has no specified value at a Runge–Kutta stage time, so it is not an admissible stage-evaluation input without an additional pointwise representative and sampling rule. This definition makes no existence, convergence, or continuous-path-feasibility claim.
lem-ctrl1-measurable-linear-ode-state-ma:
## Statement

Let $T>0$, $A\in L^\infty(0,T;\mathbb R^{n\times n})$, $B\in L^\infty(0,T;\mathbb R^{n\times m})$, $u\in L^2(0,T;\mathbb R^m)$, and $x_0\in\mathbb R^n$. Write $\|A\|_\infty$ and $\|B\|_\infty$ for the essential suprema of their Euclidean operator norms. There is a unique absolutely continuous $x:[0,T]\to\mathbb R^n$ satisfying
$$
x(t)=x_0+\int_0^t\big(A(s)x(s)+B(s)u(s)\big)\,ds.
$$
It satisfies $\dot x=A x+B u$ almost everywhere and
$$
\|x\|_\infty\le e^{\|A\|_\infty T}\left(\|x_0\|_2+\|B\|_\infty\sqrt T\,\|u\|_2\right).
$$
For fixed $A,B,x_0$, the map $u\mapsto x_u$ is affine into $C([0,T];\mathbb R^n)$, and its zero-initial-state linear part is bounded from $L^2$ to the supremum norm.
lem-ctrl1-control-box-is-weakly-closed:
## Statement

Let $U_c\subset\mathbb R^m$ be nonempty, compact and convex, and let $\mathcal U_c$ be the pointwise admissible set in [[def-ctrl1-linear-lqr-control-problem]]. If $u_k\in\mathcal U_c$ and $u_k\rightharpoonup u$ weakly in real $L^2(0,T;\mathbb R^m)$, then $u\in\mathcal U_c$. Thus $\mathcal U_c$ is weakly sequentially closed.
def-ctrl1-control-mesh-and-piecewise-con:
## Definition

For the horizon $[0,T]$ of [[def-ctrl1-linear-lqr-control-problem]], a time mesh is a finite partition $0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_N=T$ with $N\ge1$. Its cell widths are $h_j=t_{j+1}-t_j>0$ and its mesh size is $|\Delta|=\max_{0\le j<N}h_j$. A piecewise-constant control vector is $(u_0,\ldots,u_{N-1})$ and represents the measurable control $u^\Delta(t)=u_j$ for $t\in[t_j,t_{j+1})$; its value at $T$ is immaterial in $L^2$. If $u_j\in U_c$ for every $j$, then $u^\Delta\in\mathcal U_c$. A mesh family is refining when its mesh sizes tend to zero.
lem-ctrl1-weak-control-convergence-impli:
## Statement

For the data of [[def-ctrl1-linear-lqr-control-problem]], if $u_k,u\in\mathcal U_c$ and $u_k\rightharpoonup u$ weakly in $L^2(0,T;\mathbb R^m)$, then $x_{u_k}\to x_u$ uniformly on $[0,T]$.
lem-ctrl1-compact-convex-control-cell-av:
## Statement

Assume the constraint set in [[def-ctrl1-linear-lqr-control-problem]] is only the pointwise box $\mathcal F=\mathcal U_c$. For the uniform mesh $0=t_0<\cdots<t_N=T$, $h=T/N$, define $P_Nu$ on $[t_j,t_{j+1})$ by $h^{-1}\int_{t_j}^{t_{j+1}}u(s)ds$. Then $P_Nu\in\mathcal U_c$ for every $u\in\mathcal U_c$, $P_Nu$ is piecewise constant, and $\|P_Nu-u\|_{L^2}\to0$ as $N\to\infty$. This recovery statement need not hold for additional state or terminal constraints unless they are separately shown to be preserved or approximated.
def-ctrl1-runge-kutta-tableau-and-stage-:
## Definition

Let $s\ge1$ be a stage count, $A=(a_{ik})\in\mathbb R^{s\times s}$, and $b,c\in\mathbb R^s$ satisfy $c_i=\sum_{k=1}^s a_{ik}$ for each $i$. This is a (possibly implicit) Runge–Kutta tableau. On mesh cell $[t_j,t_{j+1}]$ with width $h_j$, a start state $X_{j,0}$ and piecewise-constant control $u_j$, define stage times $t_{j,i}=t_j+c_i h_j$ and the **collocation stage equations**
$$X_{j,i}=X_{j,0}+h_j\sum_{k=1}^s a_{ik}f(t_{j,k},X_{j,k},u_j),\qquad i=1,\ldots,s.$$
The corresponding endpoint equation is $X_{j+1,0}=X_{j,0}+h_j\sum_{i=1}^s b_i f(t_{j,i},X_{j,i},u_j)$. In a finite-dimensional transcription, the stage states $X_{j,i}$ are decision variables and the stage and endpoint equations are equality constraints; an implicit tableau therefore creates coupled algebraic constraints and does not require a stage solver during NLP construction. The quadrature contribution of the cell is $h_j\sum_{i=1}^s b_i L(t_{j,i},X_{j,i},u_j)$. This definition asserts no stage-solution existence, uniqueness, order, stability, or error bound. If $A$ is strictly lower triangular, its stages are evaluated recursively by the explicit tableau procedure of [[def-explicit-runge-kutta-tableau-and-stage-map]].
def-ctrl1-lqr-adjoint-equation:
## Definition

For the data of [[def-ctrl1-linear-lqr-control-problem]] and an admissible control $u$ with state $x_u$, a **continuous LQR adjoint** is an absolutely continuous curve $p:[0,T]\to\mathbb R^n$ satisfying, almost everywhere,
$$
-\dot p(t)=A(t)^Tp(t)+Q(t)(x_u(t)-x_d(t)),\qquad p(T)=P(x_u(T)-x_T).
$$
Existence and uniqueness for this terminal-value equation are established by [[lem-ctrl1-lqr-adjoint-exists-uniquely]]. This sign convention is the one for the minimization Hamiltonian $H(t,x,p,u)=L(t,x,u)+p^T(A(t)x+B(t)u)$.
lem-ctrl1-lqr-cost-is-weakly-lower-semic:
## Statement

For the data of [[def-ctrl1-linear-lqr-control-problem]], if $u_k\in\mathcal U_c$ and $u_k\rightharpoonup u$ weakly in $L^2(0,T;\mathbb R^m)$, then $J(u)\le\liminf_{k\to\infty}J(u_k)$.
lem-ctrl1-lqr-adjoint-exists-uniquely:
## Statement

For every LQR data set in [[def-ctrl1-linear-lqr-control-problem]] and every admissible control $u$, the adjoint in [[def-ctrl1-lqr-adjoint-equation]] exists and is unique.
thm-ctrl1-lqr-existence-and-unique-optim:
## Statement

Assume the ultrafilter lemma, Dependent Choice, and Hahn–Banach. For the LQR data of [[def-ctrl1-linear-lqr-control-problem]], if the feasible-control set $\mathcal F$ is nonempty, convex, and weakly sequentially closed, then $J$ attains its minimum on $\mathcal F$ at a unique control $u^*$. The direct-method branch uses exactly these three principles; Dependent Choice also supplies Countable Choice for the $L^2$ Hilbert-space/reflexivity suppliers. No use of the full Axiom of Choice is asserted.
alg-ctrl1-indirect-shooting-for-the-ode-:
## Definition

This procedure is restricted to a smooth, unconstrained-interior control branch. Let the smooth data be those of [[def-ctrl1-smooth-transcription-data]], with no active path constraints, and let $H(t,x,p,u)=L(t,x,u)+p^Tf(t,x,u)$. Supply a pointwise-defined twice continuously differentiable feedback $\psi(t,x,p)$ on an open tube such that $H_u(t,x,p,\psi(t,x,p))=0$ there; differentiability uses the convention of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]. Define $z=(x,p)\in\mathbb R^{2n}$ and
$$G(t,z)=\begin{pmatrix} f(t,x,\psi(t,x,p))\\-H_x(t,x,p,\psi(t,x,p))\end{pmatrix},\qquad B(z_0,z_T)=\begin{pmatrix}x(0)-x_0\\p(T)-\phi_x(x(T))\end{pmatrix}.$$
The **indirect shooting procedure** takes a certified differentiable IVP evaluator for $z'=G(t,z)$, an initial trial $z_0$, residual tolerance $\tau\ge0$, and correction cap $M\in\mathbb N_0$, and calls [[alg-single-shooting-for-nonlinear-bvps]] on the square BVP $(G,B)$. It returns that algorithm's trajectory and status without changing the root-tolerance meaning. In particular, `root-tolerance-met` certifies only the computed boundary residual for the numerical IVP map; it is not an exact BVP, optimality, global-optimality, or discretization-error certificate. If the control is on a boundary or no such smooth feedback is supplied, this procedure is inapplicable.
lem-ctrl1-lqr-adjoint-identity-and-gradi:
## Statement

For the LQR problem of [[def-ctrl1-linear-lqr-control-problem]], let $u\in\mathcal U_c$, let $x=x_u$, and let $p$ be its adjoint from [[def-ctrl1-lqr-adjoint-equation]]. Define the bounded linear map $DJ(u):L^2(0,T;\mathbb R^m)\to\mathbb R$ by
$$DJ(u)[w]=\int_0^T\big(B(t)^Tp(t)+R(t)u(t)\big)^Tw(t)\,dt.$$
It is the first-order norm derivative of $J$ at $u$ in the precise sense that $J(u+w)-J(u)-DJ(u)[w]=O(\|w\|_2^2)$ as $\|w\|_2\to0$.
thm-ctrl1-lqr-variational-inequality-and:
## Statement

For the LQR data of [[def-ctrl1-linear-lqr-control-problem]], let $\mathcal F$ be nonempty and convex and let $u\in\mathcal F$. Put $g(t)=B(t)^Tp(t)+R(t)u(t)$, with the adjoint from [[def-ctrl1-lqr-adjoint-equation]]. If $u$ minimizes $J$ on $\mathcal F$, then
$$\int_0^T g(t)^T(v(t)-u(t))\,dt\ge0\qquad(v\in\mathcal F).$$
Conversely, if this variational inequality holds at $u$, then $u$ is the unique minimizer on $\mathcal F$.

If $\mathcal F=\mathcal U_c$, the variational inequality is equivalent (under Dependent Choice, hence Countable Choice) to the existence of one null set $N$ such that $g(t)^T(c-u(t))\ge0$ for every $t\notin N$ and every $c\in U_c$. The pointwise condition is not asserted for additional state or terminal constraints.
alg-ctrl1-runge-kutta-shooting-and-collo:
## Definition

Take a mesh $0=t_0<\cdots<t_N=T$, a pointwise-defined smooth-data model from [[def-ctrl1-smooth-transcription-data]], a control parameterization from [[def-ctrl1-control-mesh-and-piecewise-constant-parameterization]], an explicit tableau from [[def-explicit-runge-kutta-tableau-and-stage-map]], and a possibly implicit tableau as defined by [[def-ctrl1-runge-kutta-tableau-and-stage-collocation]]. For each interval $[t_j,t_{j+1}]$, let $h_j=t_{j+1}-t_j$ and write $u_j\in U_c$ for its constant control. For any proposed start $X_{j,0}$, an explicit tableau forms the stages recursively:
$$X_{j,i}=X_{j,0}+h_j\sum_{k<i}a_{ik}F_{j,k},\quad t_{j,i}=t_j+c_ih_j,\quad F_{j,i}=f(t_{j,i},X_{j,i},u_j),\quad \Phi_j(X_{j,0},u_j)=X_{j,0}+h_j\sum_i b_iF_{j,i}.$$
Return one of the following finite-dimensional nonlinear programs, with the same chosen node constraints and quadrature objective in each form.

**Single shooting:** set $X_{0,0}=x_0$ and recursively impose $X_{j+1,0}=\Phi_j(X_{j,0},u_j)$; the decision variables are the $u_j$.

**Multiple shooting:** use $X_{j,0}$ and $u_j$ as decision variables, fix $X_{0,0}=x_0$, and impose $X_{j+1,0}-\Phi_j(X_{j,0},u_j)=0$.

**RK collocation:** introduce stage variables $X_{j,i}$ and impose the general collocation stage equations and endpoint equation from [[def-ctrl1-runge-kutta-tableau-and-stage-collocation]]. This includes implicit tableaus such as Gauss collocation: their stages remain coupled equality constraints in the NLP and are not required to be solved while constructing the transcription. Approximate the objective by $\sum_j h_j\sum_i b_iL(t_{j,i},X_{j,i},u_j)+\phi(X_{N,0})$; include path constraints only at their explicitly declared nodes.

For single or multiple shooting, check the pointwise domain before evaluating an explicit stage map; an unavailable stage evaluation returns a domain or evaluation failure and supplies no NLP candidate. For collocation, the stage values are decision variables, so construct the finite NLP and check each queried stage domain whenever its objective or constraint functions are evaluated; a failed query returns a failure status. This direct transcription samples actual pointwise data; an $L^\infty$ equivalence class without a specified representative is not stage-evaluable. For a single-shooting reduced objective represented as the finite state-step graph of [[def-parameterized-finite-state-step-objective]], its exact real-arithmetic reduced gradient is given by [[thm-discrete-adjoint-gradient-recursion]]. Agreement of that gradient with the continuous ODE adjoint gradient is only conditional on the weighted discrete-gradient representation and the separate state, adjoint, derivative-data, endpoint, and quadrature estimates in [[thm-discrete-continuous-gradient-error-order-p]]. An embedded adaptive RK controller may be used to produce a separate trajectory estimate, but its embedded difference is not a certified global error bound and does not define the fixed smooth NLP map above. The algorithm makes no continuous-path feasibility, convergence-rate, global-optimality, or unconditioned discrete-adjoint accuracy claim.
lem-ctrl1-single-and-multiple-shooting-n:
## Statement

Fix a mesh, controls $u_0,\ldots,u_{N-1}$, and a successful deterministic Runge–Kutta interval map $\Phi_j$ from [[alg-ctrl1-runge-kutta-shooting-and-collocation-transcription]]. In the single-shooting NLP, define states recursively from $X_{0,0}=x_0$ and $X_{j+1,0}=\Phi_j(X_{j,0},u_j)$. In the multiple-shooting NLP, impose the same initial state and continuity equations. Then projection from the multiple-shooting feasible set onto its control coordinates is a bijection onto the single-shooting feasible controls. Any objective and node constraints that use the same recursively determined states have identical reduced values and feasibility. This is an algebraic equivalence of the discrete NLPs; it is not an equivalence to the continuous ODE problem.
lem-ctrl1-lqr-transcription-is-a-convex-:
## Statement

Consider a finite mesh and an LQR model whose pointwise linear dynamics are evaluated by a fixed Runge–Kutta tableau, explicit or implicit, whose stage quadrature weights are nonnegative, and whose running and terminal quadratic weights are positive semidefinite. Suppose every control, path, terminal, initial, and shooting/collocation constraint is specified by finitely many affine equalities or inequalities in the transcription variables. Then the finite transcription of [[alg-ctrl1-runge-kutta-shooting-and-collocation-transcription]] is a convex quadratic program (QP): its objective is a convex quadratic polynomial and its equality and inequality constraints are affine. This is the finite NLP/QP branch used with the convex models in [[def-conic-optimization-primal-dual-models]].
thm-ctrl1-mesh-consistent-lqr-minimizers:
## Statement

Assume the axiom branch of [[thm-ctrl1-lqr-existence-and-unique-optimal-control]], and let $u^*$ be the unique minimizer of the LQR objective $J$ on a nonempty convex weakly sequentially closed feasible set $\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal U_c$. For each mesh index $N$, let $\mathcal F_N\subseteq\mathcal F$ be nonempty, and let $J_N$ be the discrete transcription objective. Assume there are $\varepsilon_N\to0$ such that $|J_N(v)-J(v)|\le\varepsilon_N$ for every $v\in\mathcal F_N$. Assume also a recovery sequence $v_N\in\mathcal F_N$ with $\|v_N-u^*\|_{L^2}\to0$. If $u_N$ is a global minimizer of $J_N$ on $\mathcal F_N$, then $u_N\rightharpoonup u^*$ in $L^2$ and $x_{u_N}\to x_{u^*}$ uniformly.

For the control-only case $\mathcal F=\mathcal U_c$ and piecewise-constant mesh controls, the cell-average lemma supplies the strong recovery sequence. If active path or terminal constraints are present, preservation or recovery of those constraints is an additional hypothesis; node sampling alone does not establish continuous-path feasibility. This theorem is conditional on a uniform objective consistency bound; an embedded adaptive RK difference alone does not provide that bound.
thm-ctrl1-objective-and-control-error-fr:
## Statement

Let $u^*$ minimize the LQR objective $J$ on a convex feasible set $\mathcal F$, with control weight $R(t)\succeq rI$ for $r>0$. Let $u_N\in\mathcal F$ and let $v_N\in\mathcal F$ be a recovered comparison control. Suppose the computed objective $J_N$ satisfies $|J_N(w)-J(w)|\le\delta_N$ for $w=u_N,v_N$, and $J_N(u_N)\le J_N(v_N)+\eta_N$. If $J(v_N)\le J(u^*)+\rho_N$, then $J(v)-J(u^*)\ge\frac r2\|v-u^*\|_2^2$ for every $v\in\mathcal F$, and
$$0\le J(u_N)-J(u^*)\le2\delta_N+\eta_N+\rho_N,\qquad \|u_N-u^*\|_{L^2}\le\sqrt{\frac{2(2\delta_N+\eta_N+\rho_N)}{r}}.$$
The conclusion is conditional on the stated objective consistency and comparison bounds. A raw embedded RK error estimate is not a certified value of $\delta_N$.
alg-ctrl1-finite-budget-transcription-so:
## Definition

Input a finite transcription from [[alg-ctrl1-runge-kutta-shooting-and-collocation-transcription]], an initial iterate, solver tolerances, an integer outer cap $K\ge0$, and integer inner caps $R,J\ge1$ (penalty and backtracking trials). First check dimensions and domains. If the transcription satisfies the linear-quadratic, nonnegative-quadrature, and affine-constraint hypotheses of [[lem-ctrl1-lqr-transcription-is-a-convex-quadratic-program]], convert its affine constraints to the standard equality-plus-nonnegative-variable representation of [[alg-primal-dual-newton-residual-method-for-lp-qps-and-symmetric-cones]]. Supply a strictly positive primal/slack start and a dual start, then call that finite-budget algorithm once. Return its status, translating `certified-gap` only to the exact gap certificate described by [[thm-fraction-to-boundary-and-primal-dual-gap-certificates]]; a `residual-candidate` remains a candidate. If $K=0$, skip the SQP loop and return `budget-exhausted`.

Otherwise, or if the convex-QP route has no admissible strict start, use a supplied smooth SQP model builder and call [[alg-sqp-merit-globalization-with-finite-budgets]] at most $K$ times, with the given finite inner caps. An accepted step updates the iterate; any failure status is returned immediately. If an identified active set and the exact local branch are supplied, a step may instead be computed by [[alg-sqp-exact-hessian-newton-step]]. Return `budget-exhausted` after $K$ updates. The local convergence theorem for that branch is [[thm-sqp-exact-hessian-local-quadratic-convergence]] and requires its stated regularity and starting-point hypotheses.

This dispatch is a finite procedure, not a guarantee that a start exists, an NLP solver succeeds, a nonconvex problem has a global solution, or the RK transcription approximates the continuous problem to a certified tolerance. Its returned numerical residuals are certificates only when the called supplier's exact certificate conditions hold.
thm-ctrl1-local-sqp-kkt-convergence-on-a:
## Statement

Fix a mesh and a finite transcription generated from the pointwise smooth data in [[def-ctrl1-smooth-transcription-data]]. Suppose its NLP functions have continuous derivatives through order three on an open neighborhood of a KKT point $(z_*,\mu_*)$, LICQ holds there, every active inequality multiplier is strictly positive, and the second-order sufficient condition holds on the critical cone. Then, after the correct active set is identified, the exact-Hessian full-step branch using [[alg-sqp-exact-hessian-newton-step]] is well-defined from a sufficiently close primal-dual start and converges quadratically to $(z_*,\mu_*)$. The finite-budget dispatch of [[alg-ctrl1-finite-budget-transcription-solver-dispatch]] may terminate before this local convergence is realized.

This is a fixed-transcription local theorem. It gives no global convergence, and no convergence of discrete KKT points as the mesh is refined. Such a mesh-limit conclusion needs separate constraint-consistency and discrete-sensitivity hypotheses; the required page [[discrete-continuous-and-pde-adjoint-sensitivities]] has no supplied item body in this batch handoff.
